name: settings-row
purpose: One setting inside a flush `Card`: an `Item` whose content carries the title and description, with the control placed by what it needs. A typed or picked field sits in a right cell capped at the 3xs container so every field on the card ends at the same edge (`field`); a switch or a button sits hard right at its natural width (`compact`); a textarea, list, radio group or editor drops under the copy at the full measure (`stacked`). A child setting indents one or two levels under a rule (`depth`). The copy top-aligns with the control, and the description always wraps in full, never truncated. In a narrow row (below `@md` of the row, a phone) a `field` control stacks under the copy at full width; a `compact` switch or button stays at the end side beside the wrapped copy. `stackable` moves the stacking point up to `@lg` for a field that needs the full measure in a drawer-width box.
useWhen: Every row of a settings card: account settings, build settings, create pages, resource settings.
A field with a validation message under it (put the `FieldError` in the default slot after the control).
avoidWhen: A stand-alone form field with a visible label above it → use `field` around the control (`Field`, `FieldLabel`, `FieldDescription`).
A read-only list of label and value pairs → use `key-value-list`.
A navigable list row → use `item` directly.
related: `settings-group` — the band the card of rows sits in.
`item` — the row primitive it renders; place rows in an `Item.List` inside the card.
`field-error` — the required or invalid message under the control.
bestPractices: The title is the label: give the control the same text as `aria-label`.
Pick `variant` by the control: `field` for Input and Select, `compact` for Switch and Button, `stacked` for Textarea, radio groups and editors.
Show a validation message only after Save was pressed.
Use `depth` only for a setting that applies when the row above it is on, and render it with `v-if` on that state.
Let the row stack on a phone: the title and the full description on top, a `field` control under them at full width. A `compact` switch or button keeps the end side, beside the wrapped copy.

Set `stackable` only when the field needs the full measure in a drawer-width box (a long URL or a code value in a side drawer), where a default row would still sit beside its copy; never to fix a centred or cramped look.
Let a tall control (an input group of three nameservers, a textarea) sit beside the copy: the title stays at the top of the row.
Do not wrap the row or its copy in your own flex box to change the alignment or to stack it; use `variant` and `stackable`.
Do not set `stackable` on a `compact` row: a switch or a button always stays at the end side.

Keep the description to the one sentence that says what the setting does, and put the rest of a longer explanation in `hint`: the description is never truncated, so a long one makes a tall row, and the Hint glyph beside the title keeps the extra text out of the way until hover or focus.

props.name: title
props.doc: The setting name; the control takes the same text as its aria-label.

props.name: description
props.doc: One sentence under the title that says what the setting does.

props.name: variant
props.doc: Where the control sits relative to the copy.

props.name: depth
props.doc: Indent depth under a rule, for a setting that only applies when its parent is on.

props.name: stackable
props.doc: Stack a field control under the copy below the lg container of the row instead of md, for a value that needs the full measure.

props.name: hint
props.doc: Extra guidance in a Hint glyph beside the title; empty renders no glyph.

props.name: required
props.doc: Marks the setting as required after its title, as a required field label does.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The control, plus the FieldDescription message under it when there is one.

slots.name: title
slots.notes: Rich title content (a Tag); replaces the `title` prop. The `hint` glyph still renders after it.

slots.name: description
slots.notes: Rich description content (links, inline code); replaces the `description` prop.
